title: The Declining Investment
mission: Protecting your financial future sometimes means questioning an investment you once strongly believed in.
learning_objective: Evaluate concentrated financial risk, distinguish confidence from evidence, and recognise the opportunity cost of holding on to an investment.
secondary_trap: Confirmation Bias, Emotional Reasoning, Fortune Telling
guidance_level: Moderate to high guidance; strategic leadership, financial risk and long-term consequences.
scenario_text:
Over the last four years, you have invested a significant portion of your savings in the shares of a company you believe has strong long-term potential.
You initially invested because the company had a respected management team, a promising business model and a growing market.
The share price has now fallen by 38% from your average purchase price.
You have read several explanations for the decline:
Some analysts believe the fall is temporary and that the company is undervalued.
Others have raised concerns about declining margins, increasing debt and stronger competition.
The company's management continues to communicate confidence about its future.
A few investors who previously supported the company have started reducing their holdings.
You have enough savings to manage your regular expenses, but this investment represents a substantial portion of the money you had set aside for a future property purchase.
You now face a difficult choice.
Selling would convert the current paper loss into a realised loss. Holding could allow you to recover your investment if the company performs well, but it could also expose you to further losses and delay your property plans.
You are not required to recover your original purchase price. You need to decide what makes financial sense from today onwards.

title: The Commercial Property Purchase
